comment: Seed for scripts/workstream-lock.mjs — the CLI-first task DAG for design v0.8, specified in docs/confit-v0.8-task-dag.md. `phase` is P0 for foundation tasks, otherwise the owning lane (K kernel, M memory, L llm, X cli, S data, N nudge, G guards, U ui). This is the whole registry: the v0.3-era seed in confit-tasks.seed.json has been wiped and must not be re-registered. Read the task spec in the DAG doc before claiming — the title is a label, not the spec.

P0.1.title: Repo bootstrap, CLI-shaped: Node 20 + TS strict + vitest + tsx, npm scripts (incl. gate0 and gate:cli), no UI deps yet

P0.2.title: Contracts freeze v0.8: types (Read = exactly six fields, READ_KEYS), flags, module interfaces, working fixture stubs
P0.2.note: After this merges src/contracts/** is integrator-only. READ_KEYS lives here and is the single source of truth — K1, P0.4 and G1 all import it rather than re-declaring the field list. Read has no createdAt and no received_at (DAG doc §3).

P0.3.title: Runtime config, degrade flags, logger: XTrace/relay config fails fast, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is optional and defaults flags to seeded/template
P0.3.note: The optional-key rule is load-bearing: G5 requires a green acceptance run with no API key and no network, so a fail-fast on the model key would make the gate unpassable.

P0.4.title: Relay service: seven routes incl. POST /reads/{read_id}/ingest-job, write token, exact READ_KEYS validation, server-assigned received_at, oldest_entry_age_seconds in /stats
P0.4.note: received_at and ingest_job_id are server-side metadata — a body carrying either must 400. The field is oldest_entry_age_seconds, not oldest_unverified_age: the relay tracks no verification state, and since M7 drops only verified entries, every entry still present is unverified by construction.

P0.5.title: Gate zero runner (scripts/gate0.ts, npm run gate0): N=12, two re-ingest rounds, pass = all 12 retrievable, plus DELETE + verify-gone; also measures and records SETTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS
P0.5.note: BLOCKS BUILD DAY (design v0.8 §11, D-3). A standalone script, not a confit subcommand. It is also the only task that measures the ingest->retrievable window, which M7 and S3 both read — skip it and those two are guessing. If it fails, stop and escalate: the sole-store decision [E9] reopens.

K1.title: Read validator + mintReadId: closed schema checked against READ_KEYS from contracts, enum checks, weight in [0,1]
K1.note: Import READ_KEYS — do not re-declare the six field names here.

K2.title: Off-limits matcher: isBlocked(text, topics), substring match, case- and accent-insensitive, deliberately over-blocking
K2.note: Substring, not word-boundary: a topic of 'gluten' must fire on 'glutenous'. This is the gate that stops a flagged confession being ingested anywhere ([E24]) — a false negative is a duty-of-care failure, a false positive is an annoyance. Put that reasoning in a comment so nobody 'improves' it.

K3.title: Rotation: appetite curve, half-life fit from >=3 observations else seeded median, suppressions returning reason keys not prose
K3.note: Formula is plan v1.0 §3.5 verbatim — copy it, don't reinvent it. now is a parameter everywhere; no Date.now() in the module.

K4.title: Ask scoring: plan v1.0 §3.4 verbatim, calling matched() for pool(p); constants.ts holds the scoring tunables and COUNTING_K=200; stable documented tie-break
K4.note: KFLOOR is NOT in constants.ts — K6 exports it from src/kernel/cohorts.ts (privacy invariant, lives with its enforcer). Import it; do not declare a second copy. CohortStat carries no per-read signal, so compute pool(p) from the raw reads filtered by the drivers matched() returns. The allergy hard constraint from §3.4 is struck: UsualProfile has no allergy field (DAG §4 D-5). See also D-6 for K7.

K5.title: Copy linter: banned-lexicon scan (quantity, weight, calories, progress, streaks, scores, totals) with lexicon as data in its own file

K6.title: Cohort counting: census + matched at KFLOOR, deduped on read_id before counting; sub-floor cohorts returned as cohortMiss, never citable
K6.note: The motivating test ([E20]): four reads plus a duplicate must NOT satisfy k>=5; five identical-but-distinct reads must.

M1.title: MemoryClient over XTrace: ingest/search/remove, user_id a required positional parameter, explicit episode-slot reservation, pollable ingest handle
M1.note: Resolves D-2 — confirm real endpoint paths against the live API and record them in src/memory/README.md. Omitting user_id searches app-wide, so it must be impossible to omit.

M2.title: PoolStore: writeRead to confit:pool with read_id in content; readsForDriver is the per-driver counting query at COUNTING_K; inducedClaim stays top-k
M2.note: Counting and induction are separate methods ([E22]) — induction may stay top-k, counting may not. read_id must be in the record content so M7's fallback verification can find it.

M3.title: UserStore: writeProse ingests raw prose unmodified, usual/setUsual (off-limits topics live in UsualProfile), mealLog; warn when unconfirmed prose is dropped
M3.note: setUsual is the only write path for off-limits topics — G2, X7 and U4 all go through it. Do not pre-clean or pre-structure prose ([E11], §14). The prose has no relay copy by design, so its retry dies with the process; that asymmetry is intended.

M4.title: Relay client: typed routes incl. setJob, parseRead before sending, bounded backoff on 5xx and network only

M5.title: Approval write path + write guard: isBlocked -> mint -> parseRead -> relay, pool, setJob (best-effort), prose; blocked writes nothing anywhere
M5.note: Write ORDER is a correctness requirement: relay first, because the relay entry is the record M7 re-ingests from. Pool-first loses a read on a crash; relay-first risks only a duplicate, which K6 dedups. This isBlocked check is the authoritative one ([E24] §9 fix, covers the prose too) — L2's earlier check is an optimisation; keep both. Owns src/memory/guard.ts, which G1 tests.

M6.title: PoolView: pool union relay for a driver deduped on read_id; under pool=relay-only serve data/seeds/induction-set.json plus relay and return degraded
M6.note: Depends on S2 because the relay-only induction set is an S2 artifact.

M7.title: Settle-sweeper: verify each entry older than SETTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS, drop if retrievable, re-ingest from the entry's own six fields if not; verified-drop only, never TTL
M7.note: Two verification paths, both required (D-1): poll ingest_job_id when present, else search the pool for the read_id — setJob is best-effort so the fallback is not optional. The never-drop-unverified test is the point of this task.

M8.title: Deletion by read_id across pool scope, user scope and relay, with a per-target report
M8.note: Front-end copy is 'deleted from Confit' — never imply cryptographic enforcement (design v0.8 §7).

L1.title: Template narrator + copy catalog keyed by reason key: reason, rotation, usual and cohort-miss lines, all linter-clean
L1.note: Lands before the live narrator — it is both the narrator=template degrade path and the fixture the whole suite narrates with.

L2.title: Chip preview on claude-haiku-4-5: structured output for the five chips, off-limits check before and after, one retry then extraction=seeded
L2.note: UI-only by design (§6) — nothing downstream may depend on this being correct, only on it being schema-valid; M5 is what guarantees blocking. A blocked topic must make zero model calls, and with no API key the module must not attempt a request.

L3.title: Live narrator on claude-sonnet-5: facts-only prompt, choose-from-corpus contract, linter gate -> one regenerate -> template fallback
L3.note: The prompt must contain no confession prose and must never cite a cohort below KFLOOR. Under narrator=template, delegate to L1 without a request.

X1.title: CLI skeleton: subcommand dispatch, --profile/--json/--yes/--help, documented exit codes, rendering separated from logic
X1.note: No business logic in this lane. Commands return plain objects; render.ts prints them. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 expected failure, 2 usage, 3 config/connectivity — a cohort miss is NOT a failure.

X2.title: confit confess: chips preview -> confirm -> writeRead, prints read_id and per-target status; consent copy states both halves
X2.note: Stub-first, but NOT claimable in wave 1: mock-start skips every dependency check, so this shows ready before contracts exist. Claim only once P0.2 has merged — you build against its fixture stubs. The [E27] consent sentence is asserted in a test so it cannot be dropped silently.

X3.title: confit ask: assemble and print the card — pick, reason line, cohort citation or cohort-miss, rotation/usual lines, degraded disclosure, runners-up, full score map under --json
X3.note: Stub-first, but NOT claimable in wave 1: mock-start skips every dependency check, so this shows ready before contracts exist. Claim only once P0.2 has merged. Acceptance runs against the P0.2 fixture pool, NOT the S2 seed — the seed-based near-tie assertion is G4's, and keeping them apart is what lets this land before seeds exist. Never print a confession; never cite below KFLOOR. Depends on K7 (AskEngine) — assembly is kernel work, not CLI work; see DAG §4 D-6.

X4.title: confit sweep: --once and --watch over the settle-sweeper, printing verified/re-ingested/retained and oldest_entry_age_seconds
X4.note: This is the operator-run sweeper of [E21] — the thing that must work when the author's session is gone.

X5.title: confit forget <read_id>: per-target deletion results in the 'deleted from Confit' register

X6.title: confit pass census + neartie (read-only): per-driver k, citable at KFLOOR, seed-manifest cross-check, score spread and judge-read delta
X6.note: Read-only, which is why it is split from X7 and can land earlier. The census cross-check is the [E22] guard working — a COUNTING_K sized for the seed but not seed-plus-live reads must fail here, not on stage.

X7.title: confit pass mutations: provision (writes S4 profiles via setUsual), seed, reset, flags --set, nudge --arm
X7.note: provision is what makes a fresh checkout usable — without it there are no profiles to ask as.

S1.title: Corpus: 40 hand-picked places against the Place schema with signature dishes and spice levels, plus a validator script

S4.title: Demo profiles: UsualProfile + meal log for accounts A and B, validator; B's log rich enough for K3 to fit half-lives
S4.note: This is the task the old plan called D1. Nothing else creates profiles, so S2, X3, X7 and G4 all sit downstream. B is the near-tie account, so B's profile and S2's seed are tuned together.

S2.title: Seed generator: 220 reads, every demo driver k in [5,9] across distinct places, near-tie tuned against profile B, deterministic from a fixed PRNG seed; emits reads.json, manifest.json and induction-set.json
S2.note: Near-tie target: score(top1)-score(top3) <= 0.04 and a judge read (weight >= 0.7) shifts >= 0.05, evaluated with K4 against S4's profile B. No unseeded Math.random anywhere.

S3.title: Seed loader: push generated reads to the pool scope and relay, reporting any that did not land and closing with the settle window
S3.note: XTrace has no upsert semantics, so a re-run creates duplicate pool records — K6's dedup on read_id is what keeps the census stable. Do not try to implement upsert; do warn on a detected re-run. Seeding must happen hours ahead of a demo because induction operates over the pool (design v0.8 §11).

N1.title: Nudge rules: opt-in default off, at most once per local-timezone day, permanent silence in one call, arm() for demo control; pure over injected now
N1.note: Day key must come from the device's local timezone, not UTC, or a 23:00 nudge fires twice in one evening west of Greenwich. No timers in this module. Copy comes from L1's catalog, never a model.

G1.title: Pool-write schema guard test: adversarial suite around src/memory/guard.ts asserting every pool/relay-bound body is exactly READ_KEYS, closed and enum-checked
G1.note: The guard module itself is M5's deliverable (lane M owns src/memory/**); this task is the test. Prove the guard sits at the boundary by calling the pool store directly, bypassing writeRead, and still being stopped.

G2.title: Off-limits propagation test: a flagged topic yields zero new records in BOTH tiers — no pool read, no relay entry, no user-scope prose
G2.note: v0.7's version checked only the pool, which is exactly how the §9 violation survived a review cycle. Verify the suite goes red when either block is removed, and record in the docblock that you did.

G3.title: Copy-linter regression: every template in the catalog and every narrator fixture through the linter, one case per banned lexicon entry

G4.title: Near-tie invariant against the actual seed file and profile B, plus the cohort-count cross-check against the S2 manifest
G4.note: The demo's climax is CI-protected (plan v1.0 §3.4). Lowering COUNTING_K below the largest cohort must make the cross-check fail.

G5.title: CI wiring + npm run gate:cli: typecheck, full suite, then scripted provision -> seed -> confess -> ask -> sweep -> forget -> census end-to-end with no network
G5.note: Must be green with no network and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — P0.3's optional-key rule is what makes that possible. Fails if docs/gate0-results.md records no gate-zero pass (D-3). This is the gate the UI lane waits on.

U1.title: Vite + React shell: add UI deps, routes /confess /ask /settings /pass, design tokens; imports the same core as the CLI and adds no domain logic
U1.note: UI starts only once the CLI is green. If a screen needs behaviour the CLI cannot do, that behaviour is a kernel or memory task first.

U2.title: Confess screen: textarea -> editable/strikeable chips -> Add to the pot via the same writeRead, blocked-topic state, consent copy above the button

U3.title: Ask card: pick, reason line, cohort citation, rotation/usual lines, cohort-miss variant, degraded-pool disclosure, runners-up
U3.note: Assert that no confession text can reach the DOM on the citation and cohort-miss paths.

U4.title: Settings + nudge surface: off-limits editor writing through setUsual, nudge opt-in, quiet banner with dismiss and silence-forever

U5.title: The Pass panel: census table, near-tie inspector, provision, seed/reset, flag toggles, sweeper status with oldest_entry_age_seconds
U5.note: Every action maps to an existing confit pass operation — the panel is a view over the CLI, not a second implementation.

K7.title: AskEngine: compose K4's ranking, K6's cohorts and K3's suppressions into the card minus copy, plus the NarratorFacts L3 needs
K7.note: Added after the initial seed — see DAG §4 D-6. AskEngine was declared in contracts and stubbed at P0.2 but no task built it, while X3 was specced to assemble the card in the CLI lane, contradicting §1's 'no behaviour in a front end'. Pure, so it cannot produce reasonLine (that is L3's async job): return the ranking, citation/miss, suppressions and NarratorFacts, and let the caller assemble. Owns src/kernel/askEngine.ts.
